result:
Reviewed in full. Line numbers count `#!/bin/bash` as line 1.

## Defects

### 1. The JSONL record is written before the verdict is downgraded, so the file can claim OK while stdout says PARTIAL

**Where** — lines 244–251:
```bash
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    "$(tr '\t' ',' <<<"$T0_APP")" "$GPU_N" "$CPU_N" "$VERDICT" >> "$OUT"
...
[ "$GPU_VERDICT" = OK ] || VERDICT="PARTIAL"
```

**Why it is wrong** — With `--interval 300 --out file.jsonl` on a run where `sample` failed or the discriminator matched nothing, `VERDICT` is still `"OK"` (set at line 231) when the record is appended; the downgrade at line 251 happens afterwards. The console prints `verdict=PARTIAL` and the persisted, machine-parsable row says `"verdict":"OK"` — a run missing its GPU profile filed as a full comparable row, which is exactly the claimed-outcome-vs-checked-outcome failure the header block (lines 41–47) says the tokens exist to prevent.

### 2. A missing window census never downgrades the verdict

**Where** — line 231 and line 251:
```bash
  VERDICT="OK"
```
```bash
[ "$GPU_VERDICT" = OK ] || VERDICT="PARTIAL"
```

**Why it is wrong** — Line 44 defines PARTIAL as "at least one of {drift, GPU profile, window census} is missing", but nothing downstream reads `CENSUS_OK`. If `swiftc` is absent or the census source was not found (line 86 only warns and continues), every window/offscreen/mpx column is `NA`, the `windows` and `offscreen win` drift rows print `NA` — and the script still emits `verdict=OK` and exits 0. The leak instrument produced no window data at all and the row is filed as complete.

### 3. `reading()`'s failure return is never checked, so the documented NO-DATA case is unreachable and a failed second reading still verdicts OK

**Where** — lines 151, 191, 218, 231:
```bash
  if [ -z "$line" ]; then printf 'NA\tNA\tNA\tNA\tNA\tNA\tNA\n'; return 1; fi
```
```bash
T0_APP="$(reading "$PID" "$CENSUS_OWNER")"; T0_WS="$(reading "${WS_PID:-0}" 'Window Server')"
```
```bash
  T1_APP="$(reading "$PID" "$CENSUS_OWNER")"; T1_WS="$(reading "${WS_PID:-0}" 'Window Server')"
```

**Why it is wrong** — `return 1` is swallowed by command substitution and no caller inspects `$?` or tests the row for `NA`. Line 47 promises `verdict=NO-DATA … or top returned nothing (exit 3)`, but the only `verdict=NO-DATA` in the script is the pid-lookup failure at line 127. If `top` times out or the app exits between the pid lookup and the sample, T0 is all-`NA`, drift prints `NA` for every axis, and the script prints `verdict=OK` and exits 0. Same for a T1 that fails after the app quits during the hold: line 231 sets `OK` unconditionally, so "both readings taken" is asserted when only one was.

### 4. `grep -c` counts matching lines across the whole `sample` report, so merely-loaded frameworks are counted as GPU frames

**Where** — lines 199–200:
```bash
  GPU_N="$(grep -cE "$GPU_RE" "$SAMPLE_F" || true)"
  CPU_N="$(grep -cE "$CPU_RE" "$SAMPLE_F" || true)"
```

**Why it is wrong** — A `sample` report is not only a call graph: it opens with the process path and ends with a `Binary Images:` list naming every loaded library and its path. For every app except iTerm2 the regexes are library names (`Metal`, `CoreText`, `OpenGL`, `CGL`, `AGX`), so `Metal.framework` appearing in the Binary Images list scores `gpu_frames≥1` on an app that drew every glyph on the CPU. That is a loaded-driver flag being reported as "GPU path TAKEN" — the precise inference lines 10–13 say this script exists to forbid — and it also defeats the 0:0 guard at line 203, which can then almost never fire. Separately, `grep -c` counts *lines*, not sample weights, so the `ratio=%.2f:1` printed at line 207 is a ratio of distinct matching text lines, not of frames: one hot 5000-sample frame counts 1, a cold path spread over 40 stack lines counts 40.

### 5. The per-pane block converts `NA` measurements into `0.00`

**Where** — lines 237–241:
```bash
  awk -v p="$PANES" -v r="$T0_APP" 'BEGIN{ split(r,f,"\t");
    printf "    threads/pane   %.2f\n", f[3]/p;
```

**Why it is wrong** — When the T0 reading failed, the row is `NA\tNA\t…`; awk coerces `"NA"` to 0, so `--panes 30` prints `threads/pane 0.00`, `ports/pane 0.00`, `MB/pane 0.0`, `cpu%/pane 0.00`. A challenger that was never measured is printed as the structurally ideal result (zero threads and zero ports per pane), which is the "measured zero" vs "the instrument did not run" confusion line 41 says the output must make impossible.

### 6. A stale census binary is used after a failed rebuild, while the banner announces the census is unavailable

**Where** — line 163 versus lines 174–180:
```bash
  if [ -x "$CENSUS_BIN" ]; then
```
```bash
if [ ! -x "$CENSUS_BIN" ] || [ "$CENSUS_SRC" -nt "$CENSUS_BIN" ]; then
  if ! run 300 swiftc -O "$CENSUS_SRC" -o "$CENSUS_BIN" 2>/dev/null; then CENSUS_OK=0; fi
```
```bash
[ "$CENSUS_OK" = 1 ] || echo "  ⚠ window census unavailable (swiftc failed) — window columns report NA"
```

**Why it is wrong** — If `window-census.swift` is newer than the cached `${TMPDIR}/window-census.$(id -u)` and the recompile fails, `CENSUS_OK=0` and line 180 tells the operator the window columns will be `NA` — but `reading()` gates on `-x "$CENSUS_BIN"`, not on `CENSUS_OK`, so the old binary from a previous run executes and populates `win`/`off`/`mpx`. The window and offscreen drift at line 230, which line 29 calls the only evidence that supports a leak verdict, is then computed from a census tool the script has already declared out of date and unusable, and the printed numbers contradict the printed warning.

### 7. When `pgrep` misses WindowServer the script silently measures pid 0 and labels it "WS"

**Where** — lines 129, 191, 218:
```bash
WS_PID="$(pgrep -x WindowServer | head -1 || true)"
```
```bash
T0_APP="$(reading "$PID" "$CENSUS_OWNER")"; T0_WS="$(reading "${WS_PID:-0}" 'Window Server')"
```

**Why it is wrong** — `${WS_PID:-0}` substitutes a fabricated pid instead of recording that the lookup failed, and no warning is printed. Pid 0 is `kernel_task`, which `top -pid 0` does report, and the grep at line 150 (`^[[:space:]]*0[[:space:]]`) matches its row — so `kernel_task`'s cpu, memory, thread and mach-port counts are printed under the `T0 WS` / `T1 WS` labels as if they were WindowServer's, on the very axis (WindowServer mach-port growth, lines 22–23) that root-caused the freeze. Note also that the ps-comm-basename fallback the script deems mandatory for the app (lines 119–124, written because `pgrep` demonstrably dropped 13 of 960 processes on this box) is never applied to WindowServer.

### 8. The GPU discriminator table does not cover every spelling the process table accepts

**Where** — lines 100–101 versus lines 136, 139, 141:
```bash
  kitty|kitty.app) PROC_NAMES="kitty";                        CENSUS_OWNER="kitty" ;;
  iTerm2|iTerm)    PROC_NAMES="iTerm2";                       CENSUS_OWNER="iTerm2" ;;
```
```bash
  iTerm2)            GPU_RE='iTermMetalDriver';        CPU_RE='iTermTextDrawingHelper' ;;
```
```bash
  *)                 GPU_RE='Metal|AGX|IOGPU|wgpu|CGL|OpenGL'; CPU_RE='CoreText|CGContext|CGSBlend' ;;
```

**Why it is wrong** — `--app iTerm` is an explicitly supported spelling that resolves to the same pid as `--app iTerm2`, but it falls through to the generic `*)` branch, so the same process is profiled with `Metal|AGX|IOGPU|…` instead of `iTermMetalDriver`. Combined with defect 4, `--app iTerm` will report a GPU profile off the Binary Images list where `--app iTerm2` reports NO-DATA. `--app kitty.app` likewise gets the generic regex instead of line 139's. Two rows in the same bakeoff file for the same binary are then not comparable, contradicting line 4.

### 9. The drift guard tests only for the literal `NA`, so an empty field is differenced as a real zero

**Where** — lines 166 and 225:
```bash
      win="$(cut -f3 <<<"$c")"; off="$(cut -f5 <<<"$c")"; mpx="$(cut -f7 <<<"$c")"
```
```bash
    [ "$a" = NA ] || [ "$b" = NA ] && { printf '    %-14s NA\n' "$label"; return; }
```

**Why it is wrong** — `cut` prints an empty string, not `NA`, for a field that does not exist. If the census binary emits fewer than 7 columns, or emits any stdout line that is neither `owner…` nor `verdict…` (both greps at line 164 pass it through, and `head -1` accepts it as data), then `win`/`off` become empty. The guard does not match empty, so awk receives `a=""`/`b=""`, computes `d=0`, and the leak instrument prints `windows +0 over 300s = +0.0/hr` — a clean no-leak acquittal manufactured from absent data.

### 10. Alacritty has a GPU discriminator but no entry in the process/owner table

**Where** — lines 102 and 140:
```bash
  *)               PROC_NAMES="$APP";                         CENSUS_OWNER="$APP" ;;
```
```bash
  alacritty|Alacritty) GPU_RE='OpenGL|CGL|AGX|gl[A-Z]'; CPU_RE='CoreText|CGContext' ;;
```

**Why it is wrong** — Line 3 lists Alacritty as one of the five apps measured by this instrument and line 140 gives it a discriminator, but lines 97–103 have no case for it, so it lands in the generic branch that sets process name and CGWindow owner both to the literal `$APP` — the "assumed equal" premise lines 93–96 exist to reject. Alacritty's executable is `alacritty` while its window owner name is `Alacritty`: `--app Alacritty` fails both pid lookups and exits 3 NO-DATA, and `--app alacritty` finds the pid but queries the census for owner `alacritty`, yielding empty/NA window columns. Under either spelling the row cannot be complete.

---

Lower severity, but still defects:

### 11. A flag given as the last argument spins the parser forever

**Where** — lines 54–60, e.g.:
```bash
    --app)         APP="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
```

**Why it is wrong** — `${2:-}` suppresses the `set -u` error, then `shift 2` with only one positional parameter left fails silently and leaves `$#` at 1. The `while [ $# -gt 0 ]` loop re-enters the identical case branch on the same `$1` forever. `scripts/terminal-bench.sh --app` hangs at 100% CPU with no output instead of printing the required-argument error at line 65 and exiting 2.

### 12. The ps fallback and the top parser split process names on whitespace

**Where** — lines 121 and 152–155:
```bash
    PID="$(ps -eo pid=,comm= | awk -v want="$_p" '{n=split($2,a,"/"); if (a[n]==want) {print $1; exit}}')"
```
```bash
  cpu="$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$line")"
```

**Why it is wrong** — macOS `ps -o comm` prints the executable's full path, and awk's `$2` is only its first whitespace-delimited token; for any app reached through the generic branch whose bundle path contains a space (`/Applications/Some Terminal.app/Contents/MacOS/…`), the computed basename is `/Applications/Some`'s tail, never equals `want`, and the script reports a false `verdict=NO-DATA` — the wasted run lines 93–96 were written to prevent. The same assumption in `reading()`: if `top`'s COMMAND column contains a space, `$3..$6` read the command tail, cpu, mem and threads, so mem is recorded as cpu and ports as threads with no indication anything is wrong.

### 13. `--help` truncates the output before the verdict contract is complete

**Where** — line 61:
```bash
    -h|--help)     sed -n '1,45p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
```

**Why it is wrong** — The header comment runs to line 47; `1,45p` stops mid-sentence at "always yields PARTIAL by construction: a single" and omits line 47 entirely, so `--help` never shows the `verdict=NO-DATA … (exit 3)` token. A consumer reading the built-in help gets exactly two of the three tokens it must distinguish, which is the distinction lines 41–42 say the help exists to make.

### 14. The GPU NO-DATA branch asserts a cause it has not established

**Where** — lines 198 and 209:
```bash
if run 120 sample "$PID" "$SAMPLE_SECS" -f "$SAMPLE_F" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -s "$SAMPLE_F" ]; then
```
```bash
  printf '  GPU path taken: NO-DATA (discriminator matched no symbols; do NOT read as "no GPU")\n'
```

**Why it is wrong** — `GPU_VERDICT` stays `NO-DATA` whenever `sample` could not be run, was killed, or wrote an empty file, yet the message reports one specific cause — that the discriminator ran and matched nothing. Concretely, `--sample-secs 180` is always killed by the hard-coded `run 120` timeout when a `timeout`/`gtimeout` binary exists (and runs fine when one does not), so the operator is told the symbol discriminator failed when in fact the profiler never completed.
